correctness.rationale: Definitions, boundary n=1, the two binary recurrences, invertibility, parity preservation, r=1 base orbit, and the A^3/A^6 lifting matrices are exact. All fourteen explicitly listed binary conjugation triples have rank 3 (checked from actual packaged verifier); the squaring lemma and induction cover every modulus and every primitive lift. The finite-state chain is irreducible, aperiodic (A fixes (1,0,0)), and doubly stochastic, hence has unique uniform law; aligned binary-prefix cylinders extend mixing to arbitrary X. Counting primitive triples proves both marginal residue and valuation densities. Enumeration of 8192 coefficients checks the recurrence but is not mistaken for an infinite proof. No result about other primes or a modulus-uniform rate is claimed.

value.rationale: The source sequence counts a canonical and historically studied restricted binary partition family. The 2023 paper establishes a parity property but does not determine distributions modulo higher powers of two. The theorem gives a full natural joint-residue classification at every 2-adic level and a nonuniform exact valuation law for individual counts, with the finite 21-element binary group and full prime-power lifts supplying structural explanation. It is neither a finite table restatement nor a change of variables in the prior parity result.
